# Context: types (dtype, Dtyped + derive, dimensions, ElementType, errors, crate root)

## Purpose

Runtime element-type descriptors (`Dtype` = scalar `ScalarKind` or struct of (name, offset, Dtype)
fields, plus an inner shape of <= `DTYPE_NDIM_MAX` = 4 dims; `Itemsize = u16`; `Alignment` = power
of two <= 32768), the `unsafe trait Dtyped` tying a Rust type to its `Dtype`, the
`#[derive(Dtyped)]` proc macro, the sealed compile-time element tag (`Ty<T>` / `TypeDyn`),
crate-internal shape-argument plumbing (`Dimension`, `Dim<N>`, `DimDyn`, `IntoDimension`,
`DimArray`), the `Error` type plus the validation helpers (`check_*`) and `ArithmeticStatus` in
`error.rs`, and the crate root (`lib.rs`: module layout, re-exports, type aliases). Every
reinterpretation of bytes as `T` elsewhere is justified by a `Dtype` equality check made here,
and every struct-field view trusts the field layout validated here.

## Contracts

Provided (what consumers rely on):

- C1. Every runtime-built `Dtype` (`new_scalar` dtype.rs:395, `from_fields` 476-504, `new_struct`
  569-622, `set_shape` 832-857) satisfies: `itemsize == element_itemsize * prod(shape)`; shape has
  <= 4 dims, no zero dim, product fits u16; struct fields tile `[0, element_itemsize)` exactly, back
  to back in offset order, NO padding (`check_fields` 645-685, all adds `checked_add`); names unique
  (659-666); nesting <= `DTYPE_NESTING_MAX` = 32 (649-658); layout is C-aligned (`alignment ==`
  max field alignment, every offset a multiple of its field's alignment, itemsize a multiple of the
  alignment: `is_aligned_struct` 695-706) or packed (alignment 1). SubDtype relies on "field
  offset + field itemsize <= parent itemsize" with no re-check (ops/sub_dtype.rs:98 `with_offset`,
  105 `get_unchecked`, 107-118 NdCopier over the field dtype).
- C2. `Dtype: PartialEq` (dtype.rs:897-924) compares itemsize, alignment, shape, then scalar kind
  or fields positionally (name, offset, nested Dtype). It ignores `is_aligned`. Equality is the
  gate for every reinterpretation: `check_dtype` (error.rs:159-173) -> `Ty<T>::from_dtype`
  (element_type.rs:89-92) used by `into_typed`, BlockTable (storage/block.rs:126), SubDtype
  (sub_dtype.rs:62), Plain/Transmute `element_type_change`; then `storage/scalar.rs:133-136`
  `transmute_copy::<T, T2>` after `check_dtype(T2::DTYPE, T::DTYPE)`; `core_trait.rs:122-124`
  unsafe `OperandTyped::new_input` after `check_dtype`; `block.rs:229`
  `assert_unchecked_eq!(element_type.dtype(), decoder_config.dtype)` (needs the stored dtype to
  never change after construction).
- C3. `try_to_scalar()` (818-823) is Some only for an exact scalar (empty inner shape);
  `scalar_kind()` (708-718) is Some even with an inner shape (documented 710-711).
- C4. `Alignment::as_usize()` is a non-zero power of two <= 32768 (enum-backed, 40-96). The
  max alignment reachable through safe constructors is 8 (struct alignment must equal a field max,
  scalars <= 8); larger only via a manual `unsafe impl Dtyped`.
- C5. `ElementType` (element_type.rs:16-31) is sealed (`util::Sealed` in a private module,
  util/mod.rs:28-33). For a crate storage with `ElementType = Ty<T>`, `dtype() == T::DTYPE`, set
  up by `from_dtype` at construction. `TypeDyn` (39-60) holds ANY dtype; `TypeDyn::new` (41-46,
  pub(crate), new since 6dbeb15) does no validation - callers check (Transmute: itemsize only).
- C6. `check_ranges` (error.rs:227-246, public read entries): ndim <= NDIM_MAX (checked first),
  ndim equal, `start <= end <= dim` per dim, every `end - start` fits usize. NOT the product.
  With the callers' `size.contains(&0)` early return this establishes the `Index::new_unchecked`
  preconditions at array/read.rs:232, 299, 369, 436 (storage/index.rs:40-48).
- C7. `check_get_range` (248-259) only checks ndim equality and `index.end(d) <= shape[d]`; it
  relies on `Index`'s own invariants (len <= 8, equal lengths, sizes non-zero, `start + size` no
  overflow - index.rs:13-14, `assume_invariants` assert_unchecked 98-102). Used by
  `check_out_buf` (storage/buf.rs:352-364) and many storages.
- C8. `check_get_buffer_size(size: &[usize], dtype, buf)` (269-295): Ok iff
  `buf.len() as u64 == prod(size) * itemsize` computed in checked u64 (`try_shape_product`, which
  also fails when the zeros-as-ones product overflows). Sole size justification for
  `StridedBuf::from_slice_mut` in `to_buf_slice` (array/read.rs:295 then 301).
- C9. `check_region_size` (297-312): 32-bit only, `prod(max(n,1)) * itemsize <= isize::MAX`; a
  no-op on 64-bit. `check_shape_overflow` (191-207): dims <= i64::MAX and the zeros-as-ones
  `prod(shape) * itemsize` fits u64 (not usize). `check_dtype_size_nonzero` (175-189) rejects arrays
  of itemsize-0 dtypes (params.rs:290, op1.rs:34, op2.rs:39, map.rs:235, reduction/common.rs:122,
  sub_dtype.rs:60).
- C10. `DimDyn`/`DimArray` hold <= 8 entries; `Dim<N>::vec` / `DimDyn::from_fn` / `dim_arr` /
  `try_dim_arr` panic beyond (dimension.rs:144, 262, 494; ArrayVec extend panics); slice and IxDyn
  `IntoDimension` return `TooManyDimensions` (371, 477). All of `Dimension`/`Dim`/`DimDyn`/
  `IntoDimension` are pub(crate) since #94 (22, 136, 219, 335); only `NDIM_MAX` is public.
- C11. `ArithmeticStatus` (error.rs:329-404): bit flags DivideByZero = 1, NegativePower = 2
  (`ArithmeticErrorKind`, pub(crate), 319-327); kernels OR flags in (`set_if` 355-358,
  `BitOrAssign` 393-398); `into_result` (372-391) maps any set bit to `ErrorKind::Arithmetic`.
  Consumers must carry the status to `into_result` (ops/elementwise/pipeline.rs:310, 441).

What `unsafe impl Dtyped` promises (Safety text dtype.rs:1153-1170; implementer responsible, the
derive for derived types). D1-D7 is what the rest of the crate actually assumes:

- D1. `T::DTYPE.itemsize() as usize == size_of::<T>()` (scalar.rs:136 `transmute_copy`,
  pipeline `MAX_ITEMSIZE = size_of::<T>()`, Plain byte strides).
- D2. `T::DTYPE.alignment() == align_of::<T>()` (nd_copy.rs:117 debug_assert). FALSE for the
  built-in 8-byte scalars on i686 Linux - known open K8 (hardcoded 8 at dtype.rs:955, 959, 962,
  964; `align_of` is 4 there).
- D3. Field offsets / field dtypes equal the real Rust layout (SubDtype + `into_typed::<Field>`).
- D4. Every bit pattern is a valid `T` (why `bool` is not Dtyped; `bool8` is repr(transparent) u8,
  scalar/bool.rs:20-22). Transmute is SAFE since #105 (ops/transmute.rs:17-18) only because of D4.
- D5. No padding (every byte initialized): codec/copy paths read elements as raw bytes.
- D6. The dtype is one `new_struct` / `set_shape` accept (no zero dim, shape product fits u16,
  zero-sized dtype has no shape) - enforced for `[T; N]` by const asserts (1208-1216).
- D7. Consequence relied on by scalar.rs:133-136: `T::DTYPE == U::DTYPE` implies `T` and `U`
  are mutually transmutable (needs D1+D4 for both).
- `Dtyped: Copy + Send + Sync + Sized + 'static` (1171), so no Drop.
- `Dtype::new_struct_borrowed_unchecked` (624-638): `pub`, `#[doc(hidden)]`, `const unsafe`, NO
  `# Safety` doc. Implicit precondition: (fields, itemsize, alignment, is_aligned) satisfy C1 with
  an empty shape. Only caller: the derive (jix-macros/src/lib.rs:169-176), which does NOT run
  `check_fields`/`is_aligned_struct`.

## Unsafe inventory

- dtype.rs:75-77 `transmute::<u16, AlignmentInner>` - guarded by `1 <= v <= 32768 &&
  is_power_of_two` (72); every power of two in range is a variant. Sound, local.
- dtype.rs:93 `assert_unchecked(align != 0 && pow2)` - enum validity. Sound, local.
- dtype.rs:624-638 `new_struct_borrowed_unchecked` - see Contracts. NON-LOCAL: justified by the
  proc-macro's generated asserts in another crate.
- dtype.rs:1084-1085 `ManuallyDrop::drop` in `OwnedFields::drop` - dropped exactly once. Sound.
- dtype.rs:1179-1203 `unsafe impl Dtyped` for i8..u64, f32, f64, bool8, `f16` (feature `half`),
  `Complex<f32/f64>` (feature `num-complex`, repr(C) re,im). Rely on D1-D5; D2 broken on i686
  Linux (K8).
- dtype.rs:1205-1222 `unsafe impl<T: Dtyped, const N> Dtyped for [T; N]` - const asserts N > 0,
  `size_of::<T>() > 0`, N <= u16::MAX; `insert_first_const` (util/arrayvec.rs:159-170) const-panics
  past 4 inner dims; `itemsize *= n` overflow is a const-eval error. Uses the Rust size of T for
  the ZST check, the DTYPE itemsize for the product (consistent only under D1).
- dimension.rs:151, 157 `assert_unchecked(len <= NDIM_MAX)` - relies on the ArrayVec<_, 8>
  invariant (`set_len` only debug_asserts, util/arrayvec.rs:180-183). Non-local.
- jix-macros/src/lib.rs:169-176 generated `unsafe { new_struct_borrowed_unchecked(..) }` and
  218 generated `unsafe impl Dtyped` - justified by: offsets from `::core::mem::offset_of!` (151),
  `size_of::<Self>() <= u16::MAX` (157), `sum(size_of::<Field>()) == size_of::<Self>()` i.e. no
  padding (158-167), alignment = `align_of::<Self>()` (173), `is_aligned = !is_packed` (174);
  transparent branch asserts equal size and align (198-199). NOT checked: per-field
  `DTYPE.itemsize == size_of` / `DTYPE.alignment == align_of` (trusts field impls), nesting depth.
- No `unsafe` in element_type.rs, error.rs, lib.rs, but C2/C6/C7/C8 feed unsafe code elsewhere.

## Edge-case surface

- Empty regions: `check_ranges` accepts `start == end` (also `start == dim`); `Index` cannot hold
  a zero size (NonZeroUsize), so every caller must return before `Index::new_unchecked` on an
  empty region (read.rs:207/231, 296, 366, 433). `check_region_size` counts zero dims as 1 (K120).
  `check_get_buffer_size` with an empty region whose zeros-as-ones product overflows returns
  InvalidBufferSize; unreachable for arrays that passed `check_shape_overflow`.
- 0-d: `check_ranges(&[], &[])` is Ok, required buf len = itemsize; `Dim<0>`, `()`, `[u64; 0]`.
- NDIM_MAX = 8: `check_ranges` checks ndim before the length compare; `check_get_range` trusts
  `Index`. `Dim<7>`/`Dim<8>` map to `ndarray::IxDyn` (dimension.rs:317-318); ndarray
  `Dim<[usize; 7|8]>` has no `IntoDimension` (468-469). ndim + inner ndim may exceed 8 (jix-py K89).
- Struct layout: `from_fields` stable-sorts by offset (478) and computes itemsize with
  `saturating_add` (485-487) before `check_fields`; `new_struct` keeps caller order and requires
  monotone offsets. Zero-sized fields are legal at the running offset (test 2000-2011); ZST input
  order matters for equal offsets ([a@0, z@0] rejected, [z@0, a@0] accepted).
- Zero-sized dtypes: empty struct (itemsize 0, align 1); a ZST WITH an inner shape is legal at
  runtime (`new_struct(vec![], &[3,4], 0, ..)` test 1984; `set_shape` test 1992) but not via
  `[T; N]`. Arrays of them are rejected (C9).
- itemsize != alignment: ComplexF32 (8, 4), packed structs (align 1), `[u8; 3]`. NdCopier picks a
  word type from (itemsize, alignment) (util/nd_copy.rs:30-38) and falls back to untyped copies.
- `Dtype::alignment()` is NOT a guarantee about buffer alignment: Transmute (safe since #105)
  relabels any equal-itemsize buffer (u8[8] align 1 -> u64 align 8), and a packed parent's field
  view (SubDtype `with_offset`) is less aligned than the field dtype claims.
- u16 limits: itemsize <= 65535 incl. inner shape, offsets u16; derive asserts the struct size
  (157); `new_struct` shape product `checked_mul` (581-584); `set_shape` uses
  `try_shape_product` + `checked_mul` (839-854) but the CURRENT shape product at 849 is an
  unchecked `product::<Itemsize>()` + `assert!` (850), safe only under C1/D6.
- bool8: any non-zero byte is true (dtype.rs:347). f16 / Complex `ScalarKind` variants always
  exist (archives, Python) even without the `half`/`num-complex` features; only the `Dtyped` impls
  are gated (1195-1202).
- 32-bit (x86 = i686 Linux/Windows, armv7 wheels): K8 alignment (i686 Linux only);
  `check_ranges` per-dim usize check; `check_get_buffer_size` compares in u64 (no truncation);
  `DimDyn`/`Dim` -> ndarray conversion does `try_into().unwrap()` (dimension.rs:193, 288), a panic
  for dims >= 2^32 (crate-internal). On 64-bit `check_region_size` is a no-op, so a region can
  exceed isize::MAX bytes (K64 territory).
- Recursion: Dtype `eq`, `clone`, `Debug`, `drop`, `nesting_depth`, `from_proto` recurse per
  nesting level; runtime dtypes <= 32 levels (check_fields), derived dtypes unbounded (finite Rust
  types), but writing a > 32 deep dtype fails (archive/block.rs:135, K128).
- Integer edge values: integer overflow wraps incl. `MIN / -1`; x / 0 yields 0 plus the
  DivideByZero flag (error.rs:316-318, doc example 336-345). Floats never set a flag.

## Intentional behaviors

- No padding anywhere: struct dtypes must tile the element; padding must be an explicit field
  (`_pad: [u8; N]`) (dtype.rs:176-179, 1131-1151, 1155-1157). The derive rejects padded structs at
  compile time (jix-macros/src/lib.rs:158-167; compile_fail doc test dtype.rs:1142-1151).
- Only C-aligned or C-packed layouts; arbitrary NumPy offsets/overlaps are rejected (282-283).
- Ambiguous layouts resolve to aligned in `from_fields` (doc 425-428; tests 1454, 1477); use
  `new_struct` with alignment 1 to force packed. `{i32@0, u8@4}` is packed, itemsize 5 (test 1463).
- `from_fields` sorts by offset (test 1491); duplicate names rejected by both constructors
  (tests 1506, 1538).
- A struct never equals a scalar of the same layout (test 1326); `[T; 1]` keeps shape [1] (1397).
- `PartialEq` ignores `is_aligned`. The derive sets `is_aligned = false` for every
  `repr(C, packed)` struct, while runtime constructors return `true` for a packed layout whose
  fields all have alignment 1; such dtypes compare equal and have identical layouts.
- Zero-sized dtypes exist but arrays of them are rejected (error.rs:175-189). `[T; 0]` and arrays
  of ZSTs are not Dtyped (compile error, dtype.rs:1162-1170, K53); `[T; 65535]` is (test 1957, K119).
- Little-endian only (dtype.rs:399-404); big-endian archive dtypes are rejected
  (archive/schema/conversions.rs:64-72).
- Alignment capped at 32768 (65-81), itemsize at u16::MAX (280-281).
- `bool` is not Dtyped; `bool8` treats any non-zero byte as true (1159-1160, 347).
- Derive: generic named-field structs do not compile (documented jix-macros/tests/derive_external.rs
  214-218); only `repr(transparent)` single-field tuple structs may be generic; enums, unions,
  unit structs, bare `repr(packed)` (K117), `packed(N)`, `align(N)` and multiple `#[repr]`
  attributes are rejected; raw identifiers are recorded unraw'd (`r#type` -> "type", K118).
- Arithmetic errors (#95, e6ef7ee): only integer div/rem by zero and integer ** negative integer
  raise `ErrorKind::Arithmetic`; integer overflow wraps; floats never report (inf/NaN carry it)
  (error.rs:314-318; K126, K145 marked intended).
- `scalar_kind()` ignoring the inner shape is documented (710-711).
- ComplexF32 alignment 4, ComplexF64 8 (963-964); 8-byte scalars hardcoded to 8 (K8, open,
  "i686 is a known gap" in todo.md).
- Transmute is safe (#105): reinterpreting needs only equal itemsize (ops/transmute.rs:46-58).
- Shape arguments are `&[u64]` in public APIs; `Dimension` & co. are crate-internal (#94).

## Hot spots

NEW/CHANGED since 6dbeb15 (the next hunt concentrates here): dtype.rs and jix-macros/src/lib.rs
have only doc changes; the code changes are in error.rs, element_type.rs, dimension.rs (visibility
only) and lib.rs.

- [NEW, #103] `check_ranges` error.rs:227-246. It is the only validation of public
  `&[Range<u64>]` reads before `split_ranges` (storage/index.rs:104-108, `as usize`) and
  `Index::new_unchecked`. Does every caller (array/read.rs:182, 292, 363, 429) return on an empty
  region before `new_unchecked`? The product is unchecked: read.rs:294 `default_strides_slice`
  (unchecked usize mul, util/mod.rs:182-191) runs before `check_get_buffer_size` (295) and
  `check_region_size` (300) - debug overflow on 32-bit (also in array-frontend.md).
- [CHANGED, #103] `check_get_range` / `check_get_range_ndim` (248-267) now take `Index` and no
  longer check `start <= end` or ndim <= 8. Every `Index::new_unchecked` caller is trusted
  (debug_assert only, index.rs:46); e.g. read.rs:551-554 builds a block sub-index. Is there a
  storage that derives an `Index` from another without keeping `start + size <= dim`?
- [CHANGED, #103] `check_get_buffer_size` (269-295) now gets per-dim `usize` sizes from
  `split_ranges`; `check_region_size` (297-312) gets `index.size()`. Do callers pass the OUTPUT
  itemsize where the buffer holds something wider (reduction/common.rs:495 uses the state size)?
- [REWRITTEN, #95] `ArithmeticErrorKind` / `ArithmeticStatus` (314-404). Errstate and the
  per-kind modes are gone. Check: flags are disjoint bits; `into_result` precedence; is any
  kernel status dropped before `into_result` (pipeline.rs:310, 441), e.g. on an early return
  or a chunked/threaded path that does not OR statuses together? Is `NegativePower` set for every
  integer type's `pow` with a negative exponent, and never for floats?
- [NEW, #94/#105] `TypeDyn::new` (element_type.rs:41-46) + safe `transmute_elements_dyn`
  (ops/transmute.rs:137-139): any safe-built `Dtype` with the source itemsize can now label
  arbitrary bytes from safe code. Does any consumer of a dtype trust more than C1 (e.g. assume the
  buffer is aligned to `dtype.alignment()`, or that a bool8 byte is 0/1)?
- [NEW, #98] lib.rs:383-384 `context` module / `ReadContext` re-export, 413-420 aliases
  (`PlainArrayRef<'a, T> = Plain<&'a (), Ty<T>>`). Aliases only; check nothing else became public
  through `pub use util::*` (408) / `pub use dimension::*` (404) / `__private` (434-441, exposes
  the `unsafe fn bench_util::nd_copy`).
- Derive (unchanged since 6dbeb15, core of soundness): per-field alignment is never compared with
  the field DTYPE (K8 on i686 gives an "aligned" derived dtype that `new_struct` rejects, so
  i686-written struct archives cannot be read back); nesting unbounded although the Dtyped Safety
  text demands a dtype `new_struct` accepts; repr parsing is token-string based (76-108) - can any
  repr spelling (e.g. via `cfg_attr`, or a later attribute macro) change the layout without the
  macro seeing it? Call-site hygiene of the generated `let fields_size` (158).
- `PartialEq` as the reinterpretation gate: can two dtypes compare equal and differ in Rust
  layout? Only `is_aligned` is ignored. Can a derived `StructBorrowed` with a lying manual field
  impl compare equal to a validated runtime dtype?
- `set_shape` (849-851) unchecked current-shape product and `assert!`: reachable only through a
  `Dtyped` impl that violates D6 (manual impl) - is there a crate path that builds such a dtype?
- Duplicated logic that must agree: jix-py's own `DTYPE_NESTING_MAX` (jix-py/src/dtype.rs:102,
  check `depth >= 32` at 193) vs core (dtype.rs:129, `1 + max <= 32` at 649-658) - both allow 32
  levels today; `from_proto` (conversions.rs:9-127) vs `dtype_from_numpy` (jix-py/src/dtype.rs:
  98-225) both funnel into `new_struct`/`set_shape`.

### Suspicions (unverified)

- jix-macros/src/lib.rs:158 - the generated `let fields_size = ...` binding is resolved at the
  call site: a user `const fields_size: usize` in scope turns it into a refutable constant
  pattern, so valid code fails to compile (compile error only, not unsound; the hygiene test
  derive_external.rs:79-111 does not cover it).
- dtype.rs:1162-1164 vs jix-macros/src/lib.rs:169-176 - Dtyped's Safety text requires a dtype
  `Dtype::new_struct` accepts, but the derive never runs `check_fields`: derived structs nested
  > 32 levels (and, on i686, aligned structs with 8-byte fields, K8) get DTYPEs `new_struct`
  rejects. The writer catches deep nesting (archive/block.rs:135); contract/doc mismatch.
